issues.claim: NJSBDC at Rutgers-New Brunswick resource entry: cost is 'No-cost (published as "NO-COST, 1-on-1 consultation")'
issues.problem: The quoted phrase does not appear on the cited page (https://njsbdc.com/njsbdc-at-rutgers-university-new-brunswick/), which only describes training/counselling, the virtual-only Middlesex office, phone/email and Mon-Fri 8:30-4:30 hours. No cost statement is on that page at all, so the quotation is unsupported as written. The substance (little or no cost) is real but lives on a different page.
issues.fix: Drop the quotation mark phrasing and cite https://njsbdc.com/about-us/, which states services are provided 'at no cost'; or quote the Rutgers page's actual wording on virtual service delivery only.

issues.claim: Stripe/Tidemark benchmark finding: 'median net revenue retention was 110% for multi-product companies versus single-product firms hovering around 100%'
issues.problem: The chart on the cited page gives median NRR of 110% for multi-product and 105% for single-product, not ~100%. The report's prose does say single-product firms 'hover around 100% or slightly below unless they raise prices', so the brief reflects the narrative but contradicts the printed median by 5 points.
issues.fix: State the printed medians: 110% multi-product vs 105% single-product, and note the report's comment that single-product NRR clusters near or below 100% absent price rises.

issues.claim: Recommendation 2: price the pilot 'near the low end of the published range (roughly $3,000-$7,500)'
issues.problem: No source in the brief publishes a $3,000 pilot price. The only published numbers in the brief are Skcript's USD 7,500 pilot and 'from USD 4,000' check-up, so the stated low end of the 'published range' is invented, even though the recommendation is labelled as inference.
issues.fix: Either describe the range as the consultant's own judgment (with no 'published range' framing) or use the actually published $4,000-$7,500 band.

issues.claim: ScalePad 2026 MSP Trends Report finding rated strength 'High'
issues.problem: Strength ratings are supposed to reflect sample size and relevance. The cited chapter page discloses no respondent count or methodology, so a 'High' rating rests on a sample the reader cannot inspect; it is also MSP data used as an analogue for AI consultancies.
issues.fix: Downgrade to Medium unless a stated sample size can be cited, and note the MSP-to-AI-consultancy gap in the finding itself.

issues.problem: The pricing page is undated, so the 2026 year label is an assumption rather than something the source states. It is used only as a structural example, so the risk is low, but the year should not be presented as sourced.
issues.fix: Mark the year as 'undated page, accessed 2026' or remove the year field for that row.

claims_checked.claim: Agency Core survey: 778 agency leaders, fielded 13 Nov-31 Dec 2024, margin of error +/-3.4 points
68% of agencies lost clients in the last year, up from 56% in 2023
24% cite risk of client defection as a severe challenge versus 11% in 2023
Fewer than half of agencies have formal programs to minimise client defection
Only 7% say their agency is extremely effective at growing existing-client spend; only 15% of Loyalty Builders are very effective
Agency Core report is free and ungated ('No gates. No gimmicks... completely free') and offers an interactive data visualisation
Among 165 agency leaders, 42% report average retainer tenure above two years, 30% above three years, 5% under six months and 18% 6-12 months
62% of agency leaders say onboarding access delays hurt client confidence and 60% say those delays damage the relationship if unresolved
Referral clients stayed 1.9 times longer than clients won through events, networking or outbound
Ignition survey of 273 agency managers/executives: 57% lose $1,000-$5,000 a month on unbilled work, 30% lose more than $5,000, 78% rarely or only sometimes charge for out-of-scope work
Only 16% of agencies require full payment upfront while 49% request partial payment in advance
71% say at least one in four invoices is paid late; 56% say late invoices take two weeks to two months; 84% spend 3-10+ hours a month chasing payment
Pricing model mix: 28% hourly, 28% productised/subscription/tiered, 25% project-based, 10% retainer

Promethean states that with fixed-fee/project pricing 'the bulk of the risk of these engagements lies with the agency, as scoping inaccuracies can easily erode margins', most suitable when scopes are predictable
Average agency net margin was 14% in 2024 against roughly a 16% long-run average
84% of agencies identify as specialists and specialists grew 43% faster than average in 2024
Report says specialised agencies are harder to replace and clients stick around longer
Only 4% or fewer of agencies rely on any single pricing model; the most common mix (28%) is time-and-materials plus fixed bid plus retainer
Fast-growing agencies completed 24% more projects while serving 16% fewer retainer clients than average
Promethean report is a 55-page free PDF based on 1,062 agency respondents, with reuse permitted under attribution
ScalePad: 11% of MSPs lose no clients, 45% lose 1-5%, 27% 6-10%, 12% 11-20%, 3% 21%+ a year
Client churn is the top growth challenge for 26% of MSPs; only 35% track churn as a key revenue metric; 60% have formal Customer Success programmes
Lower-churn MSPs are more likely to use structured onboarding, formal account management, monthly/quarterly QBRs and 1-2+ year roadmaps
MSPs with best-in-class CSAT are more likely to report either almost no churn or higher-than-average churn; CSAT is a point-in-time score from users while buyers are senior stakeholders

JumpCloud surveyed 612 IT decision-makers at SMEs (report says more than 600) and found 28% stopped using an MSP because it became too expensive, 26% outgrew it, 23% poor service, 21% offered more than needed, 18% unsupported products, 16% felt too small
76% of SMEs rely on an MSP for at least some functions and 67% will increase MSP investment over the next 12 months
MIT NANDA July 2025 report based on 300+ public AI initiatives, 52 organisation interviews and 153 senior-leader survey responses, 26 pages
For custom/task-specific GenAI, 60% of organisations evaluated, 20% reached pilot and 5% reached production, with 95% reporting zero measurable return
Pilots built via external partnerships were twice as likely to reach full deployment as internal builds
Top-performing mid-market firms averaged 90 days from pilot to full implementation versus nine months or more for enterprises
Buyers prioritised vendor trust, workflow understanding, minimal disruption to current tools, clear data boundaries and ability to improve over time
SBE Council survey of 532 owners of firms with 2-99 employees, fielded 12-19 March 2025, credibility interval +/-4.3 points; 58% actively deploying AI
Median annual AI spend is just under $1,000; 96% of those who deployed will continue investing and 70% plan to increase spend

Source Global: 81% of clients paid for AI consulting in the past 12 months, 99% expect to use AI advisors, 66% used small-scale testing support, 54% a limited-scope project, 71% a large project with a well-defined goal
Source Global says informal unpaid discussions were a relatively small slice of client activity

Skcript: USD 7,500 10-day US pilot, check-up from USD 4,000, 50% upfront on pilots and check-ups, pilot fee credited to rollout if started within 30 days, monthly care with three-month minimum and unpublished price
Skcript page says 'open-ended discovery phases are where budgets disappear'
Tidemark/Stripe report covers over 200 vertical SaaS companies and reports median GRR of 90% (multi-product) versus 92% (single-product)
Median NRR was 110% for multi-product companies versus single-product firms 'hovering around 100%'
Report concludes owning the primary workflow correlates with lowest churn and that cross-selling lifts NRR above 100%
